claims.text: The proposed framework integrates CALPHAD extrapolations, high-throughput first-principles phonon calculations, and uncertainty quantification.
The integrated framework will accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Mass fluctuations and heterogeneous bonding induce lattice-vibrational mode softening in high-entropy alloys.
The target alloys are derived from binary phase-diagram analysis.
The target alloys exhibit significant mass fluctuations and force-constant heterogeneity.
Candidate compositions will be selected computationally and then synthesized by arc melting and annealing.
Inelastic neutron scattering can be used to investigate the phonon dynamics of high-entropy alloys.
Compositional complexity causes lattice-vibrational mode softening that enhances multi-phonon scattering.
Mass and force-constant fluctuations associated with chemical disorder reduce phonon lifetimes and thereby impede phonon thermal transport.
Combining thermodynamic predictions with first-principles phonon calculations captures enhanced multi-phonon scattering in disordered high-entropy alloys.
Capturing disorder-induced phonon scattering will improve thermal-conductivity predictions over traditional models.
The framework will predict phonon thermal conductivity within ±10% of experiment.
The framework will improve predictive performance by at least 20% over CALPHAD-only methods.
CALPHAD-only thermal-conductivity predictions typically have errors exceeding ±30% relative to experiment.
The framework is applicable to high-entropy alloys with pronounced binary miscibility gaps and substantial compositional complexity.
The framework may not apply to alloys lacking substantial mass fluctuations or force-constant heterogeneity.
Integrating multiple computational techniques can produce cumulative error propagation.
Robust uncertainty quantification and calibration will mitigate cumulative model errors.
A deviation greater than 20% for any measured thermal-conductivity value will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The central accuracy claim requires predictions within ±10%, but falsification occurs only above 20% error. Results between 10% and 20% would violate the stated prediction without meeting the stated falsification rule.
